image_description: A Nile crocodile is partially submerged in murky water near a grassy bank. The head and anterior body are visible on the left, mostly underwater or obscured by reflections, while the dorsal ridge of the back and tail extends towards the right, covered in prominent bony scutes. Green grass in the foreground partially obscures the mid-section of the animal.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is largely submerged and obscured by water surface reflections and glare, making the specific geometric shape of the snout impossible to verify accurately.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and submerged; no teeth are visible above the water line.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eyes are below the water surface or obscured by glare/reflections, preventing verification of pupil shape or membranes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is submerged and not clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows a clear elongated structure consistent with a crocodilian.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal ridge displays distinct, raised, bony scutes arranged in rows, matching the taxonomy description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible scutes are dark grey/brown and exhibit a rough, knobby texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral side (belly) is completely submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All limbs are submerged or hidden by the body angle and vegetation; digits cannot be counted.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible extending into the background; it appears muscular and consistent with crocodilian anatomy, though the full length proportion is hard to judge due to perspective.
